title: Choose OpenFilm’s new visual world
question: Each direction makes the working editor the landing-page proof. Choose one to carry through the whole product, or re-roll.

options.label: The Mastering Desk
options.lineage: recording desks, A/B monitors, and mastering rooms
options.thesis: A photograph moves through a visible signal path from source to finished master.
options.viewport: The editor fills the hero while the image, tool channel, and export master read as one left-to-right flow.
options.risk: The console metaphor may make a deliberately simple editor feel expert-only.

raised.raise: Active state now travels across the whole interface instead of lighting one isolated control.
Every adjustment uses one repeated scale so the eye can compare the whole mix at a sweep.
Responsive layouts move complete modules rather than breaking controls into fragments.

options.label: The Color Lab
options.lineage: print calibration sheets, color bars, and professional proofing tables
options.thesis: The page behaves like a live color proof: the photograph is evidence, not decoration.
options.viewport: A full-bleed before/after proof shares the first viewport with a compact working tool rail and one start action.
options.risk: Calibration language is familiar territory for creative software and could feel expected.

options.label: The Sliding Studio
options.lineage: the Rietveld Schröder house and its movable primary-color planes
options.thesis: The landing page becomes the editor as image, story, and tools slide into one continuous space.
options.viewport: One photograph owns most of the canvas while sliding planes reveal the promise, before/after state, and a direct local-file start.
options.case: Wins both tests: the image remains instantly legible to casual photographers, and every moving plane maps to a real tool, state, or transition.
options.risk: Primary-color geometry turns into poster pastiche unless every colored edge performs a job.

options.label: The Tiled Sequence
options.thesis: OpenFilm unfolds as a sequence of image panels whose seams stay visible and honest.
options.viewport: The hero reads as three connected whole-tile panels: choose, edit, keep.
options.case: The panel sequence clarifies the three-step workflow, but the decorative lineage is less immediate for modern photo editing.
options.risk: Pattern borders could compete with the photograph and slow the first action.

options.label: The One-Bit Desktop
options.lineage: early monochrome desktop publishing and image tools
options.thesis: OpenFilm is an instantly recognizable editor made from crisp windows, dithers, and reversible direct manipulation.
options.viewport: A single overlapping editor window demonstrates selection, crop, and export without leaving the hero.
options.case: The interface reads immediately, but the retro desktop identity would speak louder than the user’s photography.
options.risk: Novelty and nostalgia could overpower accessibility and photographic fidelity.

options.label: Living Color Skin
options.lineage: cephalopod chromatophores and traveling skin signals
options.thesis: Every edit ripples visibly across the whole product surface.
options.viewport: The hero image and controls share one responsive living texture whose color state changes with the selected look.
options.case: The state language is rich, but the biological metaphor obscures local photo editing instead of explaining it.
options.risk: Organic motion would distract from precise tools and reduced-motion users.
options.kept: State should travel across the interface, not live in isolated controls.

options.label: The Meter Bridge
options.lineage: ballistic VU meters across an analog recording desk
options.thesis: Every adjustment remains comparable in one repeated instrument row.
options.viewport: A broad row of adjustment meters sits beneath one before/after image monitor.
options.case: The sweeping comparison is useful, but it duplicates the assigned mastering world without solving its expert-tool risk.
options.risk: Too many instruments would inflate visual density and cognitive load.
options.kept: Repeated scales let the eye compare the full adjustment state at a sweep.

options.label: The Opening Cabinet
options.lineage: chaekgeori bookshelf paintings in reverse perspective
options.thesis: Tool groups open toward the photographer as complete, inspectable boxes.
options.viewport: A shelf-like grid holds the image, three tool groups, and export as complete modules that widen on focus.
options.case: Whole-box reflow is disciplined, but the inventory metaphor makes a fast editor feel like a collection to browse.
options.risk: Reverse perspective would fight the image’s own geometry and create spatial confusion.
options.kept: Every responsive module should remain a complete whole rather than a fractional leftover.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark editor shell with a centered hero, rounded screenshot, and feature cards.
canonCard.viewport: Centered headline and CTA above a framed editor screenshot, followed by a three-card feature grid.
canonCard.risk: Clear and competent, but indistinguishable from the editors OpenFilm should outgrow.
